subject: Culture
title: Tattoos as Cultural Dress
description: A short lesson to help you apply Tattoos as Cultural Dress.

hook.text: Ötzi the Iceman, frozen 5,300 years ago, had 61 tattoos. They were placed on acupuncture points for pain relief.

buildup.text: Tattoos are permanent clothing. Polynesian 'tatau' marked identity, rank, and life achievements on the skin.

discovery.text: Japanese 'irezumi' was both art and punishment. Criminals were tattooed as marks of shame; warriors wore them as pride.

twist.text: Western sailors brought tattoos from Polynesia. What was sacred ritual became carnival novelty—then became art again.

climax.text: Today 40% of American millennials have tattoos. The permanent mark became mainstream self-expression.

punchline.text: Tattoos are the oldest clothing that never comes off.

quiz.question: How many tattoos did Ötzi the Iceman have?
